verses.original: Μὴ πολλοὶ διδάσκαλοι γίνεσθε ἀδελφοί μου εἰδότες ὅτι μεῖζον κρίμα λημψόμεθα
verses.transliteration: Mē polloi didaskaloi ginesthe adelphoi mou eidotes hoti meizon krima lēmpsometha
verses.literal: Not many of you should become teachers my brothers because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly

verses.original: πολλὰ γὰρ πταίομεν ἅπαντες εἴ τις ἐν λόγῳ οὐ πταίει οὗτος τέλειος ἀνήρ δυνατὸς χαλιναγωγῆσαι καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα
verses.transliteration: polla gar ptaiomen hapantes ei tis en logō ou ptaiei houtos teleios anēr dynatos chalinagōgēsai kai holon to sōma
verses.literal: We all stumble in many ways If anyone is never at fault in what he says he is a perfect man able to control his whole body

verses.original: Εἰ δὲ τῶν ἵππων τοὺς χαλινοὺς εἰς τὰ στόματα βάλλομεν εἰς τὸ πείθεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα αὐτῶν μετάγομεν
verses.transliteration: Ei de tōn hippōn tous chalinous eis ta stomata ballomen eis to peithesthai autous hēmin kai holon to sōma autōn metagomen
verses.literal: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us we can guide the whole animal

verses.original: ἰδοὺ καὶ τὰ πλοῖα τηλικαῦτα ὄντα καὶ ὑπὸ ἀνέμων σκληρῶν ἐλαυνόμενα μετάγεται ὑπὸ ἐλαχίστου πηδαλίου ὅπου ἡ ὁρμὴ τοῦ εὐθύνοντος βούλεται
verses.transliteration: idou kai ta ploia tēlikauta onta kai hypo anemōn sklērōn elaunomena metagetai hypo elachistou pēdaliou hopou hē hormē tou euthynontos bouletai
verses.literal: Consider ships as well Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined . . .

verses.original: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα μικρὸν μέλος ἐστὶν καὶ μεγάλα αὐχεῖ ἰδοὺ ἡλίκον πῦρ ἡλίκην ὕλην ἀνάπτει
verses.transliteration: Houtōs kai hē glōssa mikron melos estin kai megala auchei idou hēlikon pyr hēlikēn hylēn anaptei
verses.literal: In the same way . . . the tongue is a small part of the body but it boasts of great things Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze

verses.original: καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα πῦρ ὁ κόσμος τῆς ἀδικίας ἡ γλῶσσα καθίσταται ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν ἡ σπιλοῦσα ὅλον τὸ σῶμα καὶ φλογίζουσα τὸν τροχὸν τῆς γενέσεως καὶ φλογιζομένη ὑπὸ τῆς γεέννης
verses.transliteration: kai hē glōssa pyr ho kosmos tēs adikias hē glōssa kathistatai en tois melesin hēmōn hē spilousa holon to sōma kai phlogizousa ton trochon tēs geneseōs kai phlogizomenē hypo tēs geennēs
verses.literal: The tongue also is a fire a world of wickedness - among the parts of the body It pollutes the whole person sets the course of his life on fire and is itself set on fire by hell

verses.original: Πᾶσα γὰρ φύσις θηρίων τε καὶ πετεινῶν ἑρπετῶν τε καὶ ἐναλίων δαμάζεται καὶ δεδάμασται τῇ φύσει τῇ ἀνθρωπίνῃ
verses.transliteration: Pasa gar physis thēriōn te kai peteinōn herpetōn te kai enaliōn damazetai kai dedamastai tē physei tē anthrōpinē
verses.literal: All kinds of animals birds reptiles and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man . . .

verses.original: τὴν δὲ γλῶσσαν οὐδεὶς δαμάσαι δύναται ἀνθρώπων ἀκατάστατον κακόν μεστὴ ἰοῦ θανατηφόρου
verses.transliteration: tēn de glōssan oudeis damasai dynatai anthrōpōn akatastaton kakon mestē iou thanatēphorou
verses.literal: but no man can tame the tongue It is a restless evil full of deadly poison

verses.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν Κύριον καὶ Πατέρα καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ καταρώμεθα τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ γεγονότας
verses.transliteration: En autē eulogoumen ton Kyrion kai Patera kai en autē katarōmetha tous anthrōpous tous kath’ homoiōsin Theou gegonotas
verses.literal: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father and with it we curse men who have been made in God’s likeness

verses.original: ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ στόματος ἐξέρχεται εὐλογία καὶ κατάρα οὐ χρή ἀδελφοί μου ταῦτα οὕτως γίνεσθαι
verses.transliteration: ek tou autou stomatos exerchetai eulogia kai katara ou chrē adelphoi mou tauta houtōs ginesthai
verses.literal: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing My brothers this should not be

verses.original: μήτι ἡ πηγὴ ἐκ τῆς αὐτῆς ὀπῆς βρύει τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ τὸ πικρόν
verses.transliteration: mēti hē pēgē ek tēs autēs opēs bryei to glyky kai to pikron
verses.literal: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same - spring

verses.original: μὴ δύναται ἀδελφοί μου συκῆ ἐλαίας ποιῆσαι ἢ ἄμπελος σῦκα οὔτε ἁλυκὸν γλυκὺ ποιῆσαι ὕδωρ
verses.transliteration: mē dynatai adelphoi mou sykē elaias poiēsai ē ampelos syka oute halykon glyky poiēsai hydōr
verses.literal: My brothers can a fig tree grow olives or a grapevine bear figs Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water

verses.original: Τίς σοφὸς καὶ ἐπιστήμων ἐν ὑμῖν δειξάτω ἐκ τῆς καλῆς ἀναστροφῆς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἐν πραΰτητι σοφίας
verses.transliteration: Tis sophos kai epistēmōn en hymin deixatō ek tēs kalēs anastrophēs ta erga autou en prautēti sophias
verses.literal: Who is wise and understanding among you Let him show it by his good conduct by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ζῆλον πικρὸν ἔχετε καὶ ἐριθείαν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν μὴ κατακαυχᾶσθε καὶ ψεύδεσθε κατὰ τῆς ἀληθείας
verses.transliteration: ei de zēlon pikron echete kai eritheian en tē kardia hymōn mē katakauchasthe kai pseudesthe kata tēs alētheias
verses.literal: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts do not boast in it or deny . . . the truth

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν αὕτη ἡ σοφία ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη ἀλλὰ ἐπίγειος ψυχική δαιμονιώδης
verses.transliteration: ouk estin hautē hē sophia anōthen katerchomenē alla epigeios psychikē daimoniōdēs
verses.literal: Such wisdom does not come from above but is earthly unspiritual demonic

verses.original: ὅπου γὰρ ζῆλος καὶ ἐριθεία ἐκεῖ ἀκαταστασία καὶ πᾶν φαῦλον πρᾶγμα
verses.transliteration: hopou gar zēlos kai eritheia ekei akatastasia kai pan phaulon pragma
verses.literal: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist there will be disorder and every evil practice

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ ἄνωθεν σοφία πρῶτον μὲν ἁγνή ἐστιν ἔπειτα εἰρηνική ἐπιεικής εὐπειθής μεστὴ ἐλέους καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν ἀδιάκριτος ἀνυπόκριτος
verses.transliteration: Hē de anōthen sophia prōton men hagnē estin epeita eirēnikē epieikēs eupeithēs mestē eleous kai karpōn agathōn adiakritos anypokritos
verses.literal: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure then peace-loving gentle accommodating full of mercy and good fruit impartial and sincere

verses.original: καρπὸς δὲ δικαιοσύνης ἐν εἰρήνῃ σπείρεται τοῖς ποιοῦσιν εἰρήνην
verses.transliteration: karpos de dikaiosynēs en eirēnē speiretai tois poiousin eirēnēn
verses.literal: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness
